title: Normalize usage entropy and sequential retry dedupe for billing exports
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: We are seeing sporadic invoice discrepancies caused by two correlated issues: (1) non-deterministic ordering in the hourly usage rollup (usage entropy) which leads to different export signatures across runs, and (2) duplicate lines created when sequential retries of ingestion or downstream webhook replays lack a stable idempotency key. Together these produce duplicate or missing invoice lines for a small but high-noise subset of customers, especially around plan swaps and rollback flows.

Background and root cause hypotheses: 
- The hourly aggregator groups events using a map iteration order that varies across JVM runs and at high cardinality, producing non-deterministic line merging.
- Retry storms (e.g., network flaps) re-ingest identical events without a durable dedupe key; downstream exporters re-emit lines with slight timestamp jitter, creating near-duplicates that the reconciler currently treats as distinct.
- Plan-swap rollbacks generate credit adjustments that are sometimes emitted as separate negative line items instead of reassigning to the original invoice line, confusing NetSuite export matching and Proration logic.

Goals: 
1) Produce deterministic, stable export signatures so repeated runs of the export are idempotent and comparable.
2) Ensure sequential retry deduplication at the ledger/export boundary to prevent duplicate invoice lines.
3) Canonicalize handling of rollback credit adjustments so proration for plan swaps is correctly attributed.
4) Provide a safe reprocessing path and metrics to monitor duplicate-line regressions and the net invoice delta introduced by fixes.

Proposed approach: 
- Deterministic sort key: canonicalize usage aggregation sort order by (customer_id, meter_id, event_ts, ingestion_sequence) prior to any map/reduce pass. 
- Export signature: compute an export_signature = sha256(ledger_version + canonicalized_line_contents) that is persisted alongside export lines. Repeat exports with same ledger_version must yield identical signatures.
- Idempotency: introduce export_idempotency_key derived from (customer_id, ledger_version, export_signature) and enforce dedupe in the NetSuite/Stripe exporter.
- Rollback handling: detect rollback events via the existing plan_swap audit trail and apply them as attribute updates to existing invoice lines (preferred) or emit a single corrective line with a stable reference to the original line.
- Replayer/backfill: implement an event-sourced replayer that can reprocess a single hourly window deterministically using the canonical sort and write a reconciliation delta file for audit + dry-run mode.
- Tests and monitoring: unit tests for canonicalization, integration tests against a NetSuite export sandbox, canary on a 2% customer shard, and dashboards tracking "duplicate_lines_count", "export_signature_variance", and "invoice_total_delta".

Acceptance criteria: 
- Repeated exports for the same ledger_version produce identical export_signature for all test accounts.
- Canary run on 2% of traffic shows <0.01% increase in invoice discrepancies and no increase in latency beyond the SLA.
- The replayer can produce a dry-run reconciliation report for any historic hourly window with deterministic output.
- At least one NetSuite sandbox end-to-end test demonstrates correct attribution of credits for a plan-swap rollback scenario.

Rollout plan: 
1) Implement deterministic sort and export_signature in a feature branch. Unit + integration tests.
2) Add idempotency enforcement in exporter; run local NetSuite sandbox tests.
3) Deploy exporter changes to staging; run replayer on recent windows and inspect reconciliation reports.
4) Canary export for 2% of customers for 48 hours; monitor metrics & support queue.
5) Full rollout if canary metrics pass; otherwise rollback and iterate.

Risks and mitigations: 
- Risk: Export signature mismatch due to floating-point or serialization differences. Mitigation: canonical JSON encoder + stable numeric formatting.
- Risk: Replayer write could cause double-charges if misconfigured. Mitigation: replayer defaults to dry-run and explicit confirm-to-apply flag; writes to a quarantine export stream until manual approval.

Artifacts and links: 
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/BILL/Deterministic+Billing+Export+Design 
- Spike notes (ordering experiment): https://docs.google.com/document/d/1-example-spike 
- Draft PR for aggregator canonical sort: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/4826 

Notes: This ticket focuses strictly on deterministic export signatures and sequential retry dedupe; separate follow-ups should handle multi-currency rounding alignment and quota-apportionment changes.
comments: 2025-01-13 - Triage: Aisha ran initial query to quantify affected accounts; ~0.18% customers have at least one export_signature mismatch in the last 90 days. Info in spreadsheet: https://drive.google.com/example-report
2025-01-16 - Spike: Marcus completed a memory/latency profile of the canonical sort; overhead is ~4% CPU for peak hourly aggregates. CPU budget approved by infra team.

2025-01-20 - Design review: PM (Riley Chen) and Eng Leads reviewed approach; requested explicit dry-run for replayer and extra NetSuite sandbox tests. Action: add quarantine export stream. Decision: proceed with PR for canonical sort first.

2025-01-24 - PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/4826 - includes deterministic serializer and canonical sort implementation. Ran unit tests for stable ordering across multiple JVM versions.

2025-01-28 - QA: Integration test against NetSuite sandbox shows correct signature stability but surfaced an edge-case where meter_id collisions in the ingest pipeline cause identical signatures across different meters. Action: include ingestion_sequence in sort key; Marcus to update PR.
2025-01-30 - Updated PR with ingestion_sequence and idempotency_key enforcement. Requested review from @kate and @omar.
2025-02-01 - Code review: @kate approved with minor comments on logging. Added integration test that simulates plan-swap rollback and verifies attribution of credit to original line.

2025-02-03 - Canary scheduled: Plan to run 2% shard starting 2025-02-05 for 48 hours. Monitoring dashboards and alert thresholds configured. Next: finalize replayer dry-run and NetSuite sandbox full pass.
